decisions.reason: Requesting a more robust field representation does not change the required placeholder-clearing behavior.
The architecture-quality change does not alter the independent requirement for interactive-field help labels.
The client requests a more robust field architecture but does not select or remove any visual discoverability cue, so the existing unresolved visual-cue state remains unchanged.
The reference to unsuitable legacy developer fields concerns text-entry controls, not transfer of content from legacy templates.
The text-entry architecture change does not affect bullet sizing, alignment, balance, reference design, or color.
The source decision concerns text-entry field representation and does not change Tab-based list hierarchy behavior.
The requested robustness applies to text-entry fields, not table or column behavior during paste.
Changing text-entry field architecture does not alter the required language of style names.
The source decision does not change the requirement to include the customer's theme colors.
The text-entry architecture change does not modify any named-style typography requirement.
